policy_title: Drive Innovation, Regulate AI, and Support Diverse Business Models
stated: Labour will support AI sector development by removing planning barriers for datacentres and creating a National Data Library for data-driven public services with safeguards. They will introduce ten-year budgets for R&D institutions, create a new Regulatory Innovation Office to streamline regulation for new technologies, and introduce binding regulation on powerful AI models while banning sexually explicit deepfakes. The party also aims to double the UK's co-operative and mutuals sector.

source.quote: Labour will ensure our industrial strategy supports the development of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) sector, removes planning barriers to new datacentres. And we will create a National Data Library to bring together existing research programmes and help deliver data-driven public services, whilst maintaining strong safeguards and ensuring all of the public benefit. Labour will scrap short funding cycles for key R&D institutions in favour of ten-year budgets that allow meaningful partnerships with industry to keep the UK at the forefront of global innovation. Labour will create a new Regulatory Innovation Office, bringing together existing functions across government. This office will help regulators update regulation, speed up approval timelines, and co-ordinate issues that span existing boundaries. Labour will ensure the safe development and use of AI models by introducing binding regulation on the handful of companies developing the most powerful AI models and by banning the creation of sexually explicit deepfakes. Labour will support diverse business models which bring innovation and new products to the market. This includes the co-operative sector, and we will aim to double the size of the UK’s co-operative and mutuals sector.

bearing_set.reason: Banning sexually explicit deepfakes directly concerns privacy and equal treatment (a measure targeting a harm overwhelmingly affecting women); binding AI model regulation touches civil liberties, due process, and data-privacy rights — squarely within O9's legal/civil-rights scope.

Explicitly doubling the UK co-operative and mutuals sector is a direct intervention in business ownership models that affects worker governance, pay distribution, and employment security for those in the sector — earns a real verdict on work quality and fair pay.
Banning sexually explicit deepfakes creates a new criminal offence directly targeting a form of harm to victims, moving crime rates and justice indicators.

Removing planning barriers for datacentres, ten-year R&D budgets, and a Regulatory Innovation Office directly target productivity, business investment, and economic dynamism — the core indicators of aggregate prosperity.

Banning sexually explicit deepfakes is a concrete restriction on content creation (free expression); binding regulation on powerful AI models and a National Data Library with 'safeguards' raise privacy/surveillance questions — both bearing on personal liberty indicators.
Co-operative expansion redistributes business ownership and profits to member-workers rather than external shareholders, providing a concrete mechanism to narrow the wealth and income gap.

membership_note: Policy spans four genuine bearings: an aggregate-prosperity play (AI/R&D/deregulation → O13), a labour-quality structural change (co-operatives → O4), a liberty/privacy dimension (deepfake ban and AI regulation → O10), and an inequality dimension (co-operative ownership model → O14). Environmental effects from datacentres are real but too indirect and energy-source-dependent to clear the non-negligible bar under O6. Public-finance effects of R&D budgets are unspecified in funding source and do not clearly bear on O12 beyond a generic cost.
